bug_semantics: Unauthenticated Magento GraphQL (frontName graphql) accepts a query document and executes it through QueryProcessor::process without bounding field aliases. An attacker POSTs a document that aliases expensive operations (for example many products selections) so each alias independently runs a costly resolver. Pre-fix production-mode checks only ran QueryComplexityLimiter::validateFieldCount plus webonyx QueryComplexity/QueryDepth (defaults queryComplexity=1000, queryDepth=20), which still allow a large number of aliased root fields under the field budget and do not stop alias-driven resource exhaustion. That is CWE-20 improper input validation leading to application DoS (CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, no admin). APSB25-71 added validateAliasCount (default maximum_alias_allowed=10) as a preliminary check before those validators.
flaw_origin: The first public write of the mechanism is MAGETWO-81033 commit d551d1e3f70f8ae09c4de6958125f22b855d5569 (2017-10-25), which added Magento\GraphQl\Controller\GraphQl::dispatch calling GraphQL::execute on the attacker-supplied query string with no alias or complexity bound. Immediate parent 9ed7081088dcc2bf216aa374d43b2e8b7472160d has no app/code/Magento/GraphQl tree and no GraphQL::execute. QueryProcessor (bede1a878bca463301cb50569af6d6eda018bcdb) is a later extract/refactor of that execute path; QueryComplexityLimiter and validateFieldCount are later incomplete mitigations, not first-write. The surviving hole is unbounded GraphQL aliases on that execute path until AC-14323.

reasoning: Adobe CVE-2025-49554 / GHSA-xgfm-992v-h2hr is a published CWE-20 unauthenticated application DoS, not withdrawn. Comparing the APSB25-71 Magento Open Source patches, the only unauthenticated input-validation DoS fix is GraphQL alias limiting: QueryProcessor began calling QueryComplexityLimiter::validateAliasCount so a query with more than maximum_alias_allowed aliases is rejected before field-count and DocumentValidator work, matching the limiter comment that a large alias count consumes substantial resources. Attack path is POST /graphql (frontName graphql) with a crafted document; no login or user interaction. The BIC is the 2017 GraphQL front controller that first executed attacker-controlled query text; the parent lacks that module and any GraphQL::execute. Later QueryProcessor/complexity-limiter commits refactored or partially mitigated the same path and are not BICs. Tag check: BIC precedes all listed affected 2.4.x lines; the alias check is absent on 2.4.8-p1/2.4.9-alpha1/2.4.7-p6/2.4.6-p11 and present on the patched tags. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object, which is a 2017 Magento engineer commit with no AI authorship markers, so NOT_AI.
